04d67b50: In what year did the French Revolution break out?
The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on July 14, ending the Ancien Régime.
402c8546: Who was pharaoh when the Great Pyramid of Giza was built?
Khufu (Cheops) is the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh who had the Great Pyramid built around 2560 BC.
6f0c1782: Which battle marked Napoleon's final defeat in 1815?
The Battle of Waterloo (June 18, 1815) marked Napoleon's final defeat at the hands of Wellington and Blücher.
41d960ad: In what year did Christopher Columbus reach the Americas?
Christopher Columbus reached the Bahamas on October 12, 1492, believing he had reached the Indies.
e4536cb2: Which Eastern Roman empire survived until 1453?
The Byzantine Empire lasted from 330 to 1453 AD. Its fall, with the capture of Constantinople, conventionally marks the end of the Middle Ages.
f50bd21b: Who launched the Protestant Reformation in 1517?
Martin Luther posted his 95 Theses against indulgences in Wittenberg on October 31, 1517, the founding act of the Reformation.
139da012: Which treaty ended the First World War?
The Treaty of Versailles (June 28, 1919) ended the First World War. Its harsh terms contributed to the rise of Nazism.
5f3dfc68: In what year did Napoleon become Emperor of the French?
Napoleon crowned himself Emperor on December 2, 1804, at Notre-Dame de Paris.
c28956e6: Who was the first president of the United States?
George Washington, commander of the revolutionary army, was the first American president (1789-1797).
25740e4e: The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed cuneiform writing around 3200 BC. It is considered the first writing system.
819fc73b: In what year did the Second World War end?
The Second World War ended on September 2, 1945, with Japan's surrender after the atomic bombings.
6baeed00: Which event officially triggered the First World War?
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, set off the chain of ultimatums that led to war.
977e9e41: Which Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with elephants?
Hannibal Barca crossed the Alps with 37 elephants in 218 BC to surprise Rome from the north.
1ab94a4f: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, symbolizing the end of the Cold War.
01d48678: Who was the first man to walk on the Moon?
Neil Armstrong became the first human on the Moon on July 20, 1969 (July 21 UTC), during the Apollo 11 mission.
2d25f6d3: Which leader united the Mongol tribes to create the largest contiguous land empire?
Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes in 1206. His empire stretched from China to Persia.
51c45038: In what year did the Bolshevik Russian Revolution take place?
In the October Revolution of 1917, Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power and founded the Soviet state.
42f755ef: Which 1066 battle marked the Norman conquest of England?
At the Battle of Hastings (October 14, 1066), William the Conqueror defeated Harold II and transformed English history.
749f7eb0: In what year did Hitler come to power in Germany?
Adolf Hitler became Chancellor of Germany on January 30, 1933, appointed by Hindenburg in the hope of keeping the Nazis under control.
17fc192c: How long did the Hundred Years' War actually last?
The Hundred Years' War lasted 116 years (1337-1453): a series of conflicts between England and France over the French crown.
eee2ff4d: Who was Joan of Arc, and in what year was she burned at the stake?
Joan of Arc, a peasant girl from Lorraine who led the French armies, was burned alive in Rouen on May 30, 1431.
6a67a15d: Which French king made Versailles his main residence in 1682?
Louis XIV, the Sun King, made Versailles his main residence in 1682, a symbol of absolute power.
a565ac27: When was Paris liberated during the Second World War?
Paris was liberated on August 25, 1944. De Gaulle paraded down the Champs-Élysées the next day.
cdb06a7c: Which Greek philosopher was Alexander the Great's tutor?
Aristotle was Alexander the Great's tutor: the greatest philosopher of antiquity teaching its greatest conqueror.
779fb7f3: Which French king was guillotined in 1793?
Louis XVI was guillotined on January 21, 1793, on the Place de la Révolution, executed for treason after his flight to Varennes.
a7fb30dc: Who led the Cuban Revolution of 1959?
Fidel Castro overthrew the dictator Batista on January 1, 1959. He ruled Cuba until 2008.
c476b61d: What is the date of the First World War armistice?
The Armistice took effect on November 11, 1918, at 11 a.m. (the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month), a date commemorated every year.
d9674182: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, a mold that inhibits bacterial growth.
faf6ca5d: In what year did Napoleon invade Russia?
The Russian campaign began in June 1812. Napoleon reached Moscow, but the retreat destroyed the Grande Armée.
d57fe2df: Which 1648 treaty ended the Thirty Years' War?
The Peace of Westphalia (1648) established the principle of state sovereignty, a foundation of modern international law.
0001f9aa: In what year was the Paris Commune crushed?
The Paris Commune (March 18 to May 28, 1871) was crushed during the “Bloody Week”, with between 10,000 and 30,000 dead.
048c77d3: Who founded scientific socialism with Friedrich Engels?
Karl Marx co-wrote The Communist Manifesto (1848) and wrote Capital (1867), which inspired the revolutions of the 20th century.
492ea0f9: In what year was the USSR dissolved?
The Soviet Union was dissolved on December 25-26, 1991. Gorbachev resigned and 15 independent republics emerged.
4fa1371a: Which secret agreement of 1916 planned the division of the Middle East between France and the United Kingdom?
The Sykes-Picot Agreement (1916), negotiated during the First World War, divided Ottoman territories into zones of influence.
fb86c041: In what year was Nelson Mandela released after 27 years in prison?
Nelson Mandela was released on February 11, 1990. He became South Africa's first Black president in 1994.
f338996a: Which Roman general defeated Vercingetorix at Alesia in 52 BC?
Julius Caesar besieged Alesia with a double line of fortifications. Vercingetorix's surrender sealed the conquest of Gaul.
d27f6288: Who was Maximilien Robespierre in the French Revolution?
The lawyer who led the Terror
Maximilien Robespierre led the Committee of Public Safety and the Terror (1793-1794). He was guillotined after the fall of 9 Thermidor.
b4c55f61: In what year was Yuri Gagarin launched into space?
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961, aboard Vostok 1, in a 108-minute flight.
ae4573ba: In which naval battle of 480 BC did the Greek fleet defeat the Persian fleet?
At Salamis, in 480 BC, the Greek fleet led by Themistocles crushed the Persian fleet. The same year, Leonidas's Spartans had fallen at Thermopylae.
392ee630: Who was Cleopatra VII in history?
The last Ptolemaic queen of Egypt
Cleopatra VII (69-30 BC) was the last Ptolemaic queen of Egypt, a polyglot and brilliant politician, ally of Caesar and Mark Antony.
d45360e3: In what year was the Suez Canal inaugurated?
The Suez Canal opened on November 17, 1869, linking the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, a revolution in world shipping.
0dea6f17: Which massacre struck French Protestants in 1572?
The Night of the Long Knives
The St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre (August 23-24, 1572) was a massacre of Huguenots in Paris, authorized by King Charles IX.
e6d4b4ed: In what year did France abolish slavery for good?
Final abolition was decreed on April 27, 1848, championed by Victor Schœlcher, after Napoleon had restored slavery in 1802.
92853b5b: Which empire, at its peak, covered about 24% of the world's land?
The British Empire covered about 35.5 million km² in 1920, around 24% of the world's land and nearly a quarter of its population.
7805a4ce: Who gave the “I Have a Dream” speech in 1963?
Martin Luther King Jr. delivered “I Have a Dream” during the March on Washington on August 28, 1963, a symbol of the civil rights movement.
d881270d: Which Greek philosopher is known for his questioning method, maieutics?
Socrates (470-399 BC) developed maieutics, the art of “midwifing” ideas out of people through questions.
0af45a9d: In what year was the United States Declaration of Independence adopted?
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776, though the war only officially ended in 1783 with the Treaty of Paris.
8ea5ffe4: Which Aztec ruler met Hernán Cortés in Tenochtitlan?
Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler who received Cortés in 1519, perhaps believing in a prophecy of Quetzalcoatl's return.
87cdcded: Which international organization succeeded the League of Nations in 1945?
The United Nations was founded on October 24, 1945, with 51 founding members, to keep the peace after the Second World War.
e432a8a4: In what year was Martin Luther King Jr. assassinated?
Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated in Memphis on April 4, 1968, at the age of 39, during a trip to support striking sanitation workers.
38ec0bef: Which 1987 agreement reduced American and Soviet nuclear weapons?
The INF Treaty (Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces), signed in 1987 by Reagan and Gorbachev, eliminated intermediate-range nuclear missiles.
7c1677d5: Who led the USSR when it invaded Afghanistan in 1979?
Leonid Brezhnev ordered the invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979. The conflict lasted until 1989.
7da9ebd6: Which Mesoamerican civilization built Tenochtitlan on a lake?
The Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan in 1325 on Lake Texcoco. Destroyed by Cortés in 1521, its ruins lie beneath Mexico City.
6bce291e: Which invention by Gutenberg revolutionized the spread of knowledge around 1450?
Gutenberg's printing press (around 1450) revolutionized the spread of knowledge, fueling the Reformation and the Renaissance.
b18db86a: Who was Olympe de Gouges, and what was her contribution to the Revolution?
Author of the 1791 Declaration of the Rights of Woman
Olympe de Gouges wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen in 1791. She was guillotined in 1793, during the Terror.
db99c7c6: When was the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima?
Little Boy was dropped on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945, killing 70,000 to 80,000 people instantly.
1753bad1: Who is the mythical founder of Rome according to Roman tradition?
Romulus is the legendary founder of Rome in 753 BC according to tradition. He killed his twin brother Remus during a quarrel.
19263315: In what year was the Berlin Wall built?
The Berlin Wall went up overnight on August 12-13, 1961, to stop East Germans from fleeing to the West.
caf6fc05: Which British Prime Minister stood up to Hitler during the Second World War?
Winston Churchill was Prime Minister from 1940 to 1945 and from 1951 to 1955. His leadership and speeches (“We shall never surrender”) inspired British resistance.
091c4a54: What was Vasco da Gama's great discovery in 1498?
Vasco da Gama reached India by sea in 1498 by sailing around Africa, a revolutionary trade route for Portugal.
b4eea541: In what year did Constantinople fall, conventionally ending the Middle Ages?
The fall of Constantinople to Mehmed II on May 29, 1453, conventionally marks the end of the Middle Ages.
b16c0d7d: Which Roman crossed the Rubicon and started the Roman civil war?
Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon with his army in January 49 BC: crossing that river with troops was illegal and amounted to declaring civil war.
acf91f94: Who was Harriet Tubman in American history?
An Underground Railroad leader who freed enslaved people
A pioneer of the feminist movement
The first woman elected to Congress
Harriet Tubman escaped slavery and became a conductor on the Underground Railroad, personally guiding dozens of enslaved people to freedom.
fa933b74: Which navigator led the first circumnavigation of the globe (1519-1522)?
Ferdinand Magellan organized the first circumnavigation (1519-1522). He died in the Philippines, but his ship the Victoria completed the voyage.
1dc71429: What is the founding event of the French First Republic?
The proclamation of the Republic on September 22, 1792
The First Republic was proclaimed on September 22, 1792, ending the monarchy and beginning the French republican era.
89501d0a: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
Trygve Lie (Norway) was the first UN Secretary-General, from 1946 to 1952. He resigned under Soviet pressure after his support for the UN action in Korea.
911a4d63: What was the official name of the regime set up in Vichy in 1940?
The French State, known as the Vichy regime, was led by Marshal Pétain from 1940 to 1944 and collaborated with Nazi Germany.
10ec45af: In what year did England's Glorious Revolution take place?
In the Glorious Revolution of 1688, William III of Orange overthrew James II, leading to England's constitutional monarchy and the Bill of Rights.
726d55db: Osman I (died around 1324) founded the Ottoman dynasty, which takes its name from him, and began building the empire in Anatolia.
feaee226: What was the name of the first artificial satellite of the Earth?
Sputnik 1 was launched by the USSR on October 4, 1957. The first artificial satellite in history, it kicked off the space race between the USA and the USSR.
32c1250c: How long did the Korean War last?
The Korean War lasted from 1950 to 1953. An armistice was signed on July 27, 1953, but no peace treaty has ever officially ended the war.
cf11ee9a: Which pope convened the Council of Trent, the heart of the Catholic Reformation?
Paul III convened the Council of Trent (1545-1563), the Catholic Counter-Reformation's response to Luther's and Calvin's Protestantism.
19f099bb: Which peace agreement ended the American War of Independence?
The Treaty of Paris of September 3, 1783, ended the War of Independence: Great Britain officially recognized the independence of the United States.
70f93166: Which industrial revolution relied on electricity as its main energy?
The Second Industrial Revolution (about 1870-1914) introduced electricity, oil and steel, gradually replacing the steam of the first.
1e666a2d: In what year did the Tiananmen Square massacre take place?
In the Tiananmen Square massacre (June 4, 1989) in Beijing, pro-democracy protesters were violently crushed by the Chinese army.
09f307f9: Who was the first Soviet leader to visit the United States?
Nikita Khrushchev visited the United States in 1959, the first visit by a sitting Soviet leader, during a relative thaw in the Cold War.
a012a8f8: What was the name of the American plan to rebuild Europe after the Second World War?
The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program, 1948-1952) provided about 13 billion dollars to European countries to rebuild their economies after the war.
da4a648e: In what year was the last Russian tsar, Nicholas II, killed?
Nicholas II and his family were shot on July 17, 1918, in Yekaterinburg, on the orders of the Ural Soviet, during the Russian Civil War.
894b6536: Which Roman city was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD?
In 79 AD, the eruption of Vesuvius buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash. Excavations revealed a city frozen in its daily life.
5ea3876f: In which Greek city does the Parthenon stand?
The Parthenon, a temple dedicated to Athena, has towered over the Acropolis of Athens since the 5th century BC.
e25e4de3: Which Roman emperor had a wall built in what is now northern England?
Hadrian's Wall, begun in 122 AD, marked the northern frontier of the Roman province of Britannia.
fb4a886f: Who was the first Roman emperor?
Octavian, Caesar's great-nephew, received the title Augustus in 27 BC and became the first emperor. Julius Caesar himself was never emperor.
6aa8f80e: Which king of Macedon conquered the Persian Empire in the 4th century BC?
Alexander the Great defeated Darius III and built, in about ten years, an empire stretching from Greece to India.
e78df200: Which wonder of the ancient world stood in Alexandria?
The Lighthouse of Alexandria, built in the 3rd century BC on the island of Pharos, guided ships into the harbor.
4ed68a8c: Which king of Sparta led the 300 at the Battle of Thermopylae?
In 480 BC, Leonidas and his men held back Xerxes's huge Persian army at the pass of Thermopylae.
45c6bc60: In what year does tradition place the founding of Rome?
According to tradition, Romulus founded Rome on April 21, 753 BC.
79475dd0: Which date traditionally marks the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
In 476, the Germanic chieftain Odoacer deposed the young emperor Romulus Augustulus: the end of the Western Roman Empire.
b9ec4f26: Which emperor refounded Byzantium as his capital?
Constantine inaugurated his new capital in 330. It took the name Constantinople, today's Istanbul.
50d0416d: Which pharaoh was found in an almost intact tomb in 1922?
In 1922, archaeologist Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings, filled with treasures.
4e3fcb2f: Which stone made it possible to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs?
The Rosetta Stone bears the same text in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek. It allowed Champollion to crack the hieroglyphs in 1822.
dcde9ab4: Jean-François Champollion announced in 1822 that he had understood how hieroglyphs worked, notably thanks to the Rosetta Stone.
d1db133a: In which Greek sanctuary were the ancient Olympic Games held?
The ancient Games were held every four years at Olympia, in honor of Zeus, from 776 BC according to tradition.
6ff57481: Which philosopher founded the Academy in Athens?
Plato, a student of Socrates, founded the Academy around 387 BC. Aristotle studied there for about twenty years.
8b407c61: What are the wars between Rome and Carthage called?
The three Punic Wars (264-146 BC) ended with the destruction of Carthage. The Persian (Greco-Persian) Wars pitted the Greeks against the Persians.
7f9613cd: Which Roman statesman was assassinated on the Ides of March, 44 BC?
Julius Caesar was stabbed on March 15, 44 BC, by senators including Brutus and Cassius.
b5f23158: Which ruler first unified China in 221 BC?
Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of a unified China. His tomb is guarded by the famous Terracotta Army.
127d9644: Which army of statues was discovered in 1974 near Xi'an, China?
Thousands of terracotta soldiers, each one different, guard the mausoleum of the first emperor, Qin Shi Huang.
56d63f9b: Which king of Babylon had a famous code of laws carved on a stele?
The Code of Hammurabi, from around 1750 BC, is one of the oldest known law codes. The stele is held at the Louvre.
db223ecd: Who was crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800?
On December 25, 800, Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor in the West.
8253749c: Which epidemic killed about a third of Europeans in the 14th century?
The Black Death ravaged Europe from 1347 on, killing between a third and half of the population.
a778f5d7: In what year did the First Crusade set out?
After Pope Urban II's call in 1095, the First Crusade set out in 1096. It ended with the capture of Jerusalem in 1099.
b0ae6f11: Which English charter of 1215 limited the king's powers?
In 1215, the English barons forced King John to accept Magna Carta, which guaranteed certain liberties against royal power.
dce5f2f4: Which Scandinavian people raided European coasts from the 8th century on?
The Vikings, from Scandinavia, raided coasts and sailed up rivers. Some settled in Normandy.
79b66bd5: Which king of the Franks was baptized in Reims?
Clovis was baptized in Reims by Bishop Remigius around 496-499. Reims then became the city where French kings were crowned.
40e2a528: Where did Charles Martel stop an Umayyad army in 732?
In 732, Charles Martel defeated an army from al-Andalus near Poitiers. The battle is also known as the Battle of Tours.
789bc140: Which French king is known as “Saint Louis”?
Louis IX, king from 1226 to 1270, was canonized in 1297. He died in Tunis during the Eighth Crusade.
f949f1a1: In which 1415 battle was the French army crushed by English archers?
On October 25, 1415, Henry V of England's army crushed the French knights at Agincourt, thanks to its archers.
bbee1aff: Which city did Joan of Arc relieve in 1429?
In May 1429, Joan of Arc lifted the siege of Orléans, then led Charles VII to Reims for his coronation.
46e84973: Under which Chinese dynasty was most of the Great Wall visible today built?
The most famous brick and stone sections of the Great Wall were built under the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).
1bf148c6: Which Venetian merchant described his long stay in China in the 13th century?
Marco Polo stayed at the court of Kublai Khan. His account, The Travels of Marco Polo, captivated Europe.
2b4d861d: Which Norwegian explorer was the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole on December 14, 1911, a month before the Briton Robert Scott.
461103d6: Which Portuguese navigator reached the coast of Brazil in 1500?
In 1500, Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet, bound for India, reached the coast of Brazil, which became Portuguese.
86f0be62: Which Viking explorer is said to have reached North America around the year 1000?
Leif Erikson, son of Erik the Red, is said to have reached “Vinland” in North America nearly five centuries before Columbus.
95cdf2f9: Which British navigator charted New Zealand and explored the Pacific in the 18th century?
On his three voyages, James Cook charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia. He died in Hawaii in 1779.
2508e108: Which mission landed the first men on the Moon in 1969?
On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon, while Michael Collins stayed in orbit.
e275b234: Who were the first climbers to reach the summit of Everest, in 1953?
New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on May 29, 1953.
6bf738cc: Which Paris fortress was stormed by the people on July 14, 1789?
The storming of the Bastille, a royal prison symbolizing arbitrary power, became the emblem of the Revolution. July 14 is France's national holiday.
d6fc83cf: Which founding text was adopted on August 26, 1789?
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
The Constitution of the Fifth Republic
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen states that “men are born and remain free and equal in rights”.
d6886044: Where were Louis XVI and his family arrested during their flight in June 1791?
Recognized on the way, Louis XVI was arrested at Varennes. The flight destroyed the people's trust in the king.
82a2bab6: Which queen was guillotined in October 1793?
Marie Antoinette, Louis XVI's wife, was guillotined on October 16, 1793, a few months after her husband.
a541b0dd: Which coup brought Napoleon Bonaparte to power in 1799?
On 18 Brumaire, Year VIII (November 9, 1799), Bonaparte overthrew the Directory and became First Consul.
18482d57: What are the three days of July 1830 that toppled Charles X called?
On July 27, 28 and 29, 1830, Parisians rose up: Charles X abdicated and Louis-Philippe became King of the French.
a07cc5ab: What is the 1773 protest in which American colonists threw tea into the sea called?
To protest British taxes, colonists dumped chests of tea into Boston Harbor, a prelude to the War of Independence.
5a605ce0: Which liberator of South America gave his name to Bolivia?
Simón Bolívar led several South American countries to independence. Bolivia has borne his name since 1825.
8a0e0da4: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin, in the 18th century?
The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain, driven by the steam engine, coal and the textile industry.
0c9d3f82: Which country experienced the “Carnation Revolution” in 1974?
On April 25, 1974, an almost bloodless military coup ended the dictatorship in Portugal. Carnations were placed in the soldiers' rifle barrels.
983e02b4: In what year did the First World War begin?
War broke out in the summer of 1914, a month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo.
061d58fb: Which 1916 battle became the symbol of the Great War for France?
From February to December 1916, the Battle of Verdun killed more than 300,000 French and German soldiers.
20bac3e6: What nickname was given to French soldiers in the First World War?
French soldiers were nicknamed “Poilus” (hairy ones). The Tommies were British soldiers, the Grognards Napoleon's veterans.
94feac33: On what day did the Allied landings in Normandy take place?
On June 6, 1944, “D-Day”, more than 150,000 Allied soldiers landed on the beaches of Normandy.
1b49222b: Who made the Appeal of June 18, 1940, from London?
On the BBC, Charles de Gaulle called on the French to keep fighting Germany.
5fca7451: Which battle of 1942-1943 marked a decisive turning point on the Eastern Front?
In February 1943, the German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad. From then on, the Red Army held the initiative.
e22b891f: Which Japanese attack brought the United States into the Second World War?
On December 7, 1941, Japanese aircraft attacked the American base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
9c318b5e: Which Japanese city was struck by the second atomic bomb, on August 9, 1945?
Three days after Hiroshima, a second atomic bomb destroyed Nagasaki. Japan surrendered shortly afterward.
3a3d2c0a: Which country did Germany invade on September 1, 1939?
The invasion of Poland led France and the United Kingdom to declare war on Germany on September 3, 1939.
482e52ba: What is the name of the line of fortifications France built facing Germany in the 1930s?
The Maginot Line was meant to protect the eastern border. In 1940, the German army went around it through the Ardennes.
22a38d2d: Which British liner was torpedoed by a German submarine in 1915?
The sinking of the Lusitania on May 7, 1915, killed nearly 1,200 people, including many Americans, and turned American opinion against Germany.
b2895a94: In which city were the main Nazi leaders tried from 1945?
The International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg tried the leading Nazi figures from November 1945 to October 1946.
4d1b8bef: Which American president was in office during the attack on Pearl Harbor?
Franklin D. Roosevelt called December 7, 1941, “a date which will live in infamy”. He died in April 1945.
4152e03b: Which French king is known as the Sun King?
Louis XIV, who reigned from 1643 to 1715, chose the sun as his emblem. His 72-year reign is the longest in French history.
e698fb80: Which king signed the Edict of Nantes in 1598?
The Edict of Nantes granted freedom of worship to Protestants and ended the Wars of Religion. Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.
a719078c: Who was the first president of the Fifth Republic?
Charles de Gaulle was elected president in December 1958 and remained in office until 1969.
3bcf95fb: In what year was the Fifth Republic founded?
The Constitution of the Fifth Republic was approved by referendum on September 28, 1958, and promulgated on October 4.
d7908f9c: In what year did France pass the law separating Church and State?
The law of December 9, 1905, guarantees freedom of conscience and states that the Republic neither recognizes nor funds any religion.
8b1fbb02: In what year did French women vote for the first time?
Women were granted the vote in 1944. They voted for the first time in the municipal elections of April 1945.
6f28218a: Which army captain was wrongly convicted of treason in 1894, sparking an affair that divided France?
Captain Alfred Dreyfus, falsely accused of espionage, was sent to a penal colony. He was only exonerated in 1906.
e7a92134: Which writer published “J'accuse…!” in 1898 to defend Dreyfus?
On January 13, 1898, Émile Zola published in L'Aurore an open letter to the President of the Republic, “J'accuse…!”.
08e1a728: Which Minister of Justice led the abolition of the death penalty in France in 1981?
On October 9, 1981, the law championed by Robert Badinter abolished the death penalty in France.
9f7fef7f: Which month of 1968 is remembered for its student protests and strikes in France?
In May 1968, student demonstrations and a general strike paralyzed the country.
76aebe14: Which Florentine-born queen was the mother of three kings of France?
Catherine de' Medici, wife of Henry II, was the mother of Francis II, Charles IX and Henry III.
e6c56820: Which cardinal was Louis XIII's chief minister?
Cardinal Richelieu governed alongside Louis XIII from 1624 until his death in 1642. He founded the Académie française.
6a108de1: Which emperor was taken prisoner at Sedan in 1870?
The defeat at Sedan, on September 2, 1870, brought down the Second Empire and led to the proclamation of the Republic.
c73350a1: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
Designed by Bartholdi, with an internal structure by Gustave Eiffel, the statue was inaugurated in New York in 1886.
599d6be9: Who became South Africa's first Black president in 1994?
Released in 1990, Nelson Mandela was elected president in the first multiracial elections, in 1994.
9fdc50b7: Which American president abolished slavery during the Civil War?
Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863. The 13th Amendment abolished slavery in 1865, shortly after his assassination.
bb106b28: Which American president was assassinated in Dallas in 1963?
John F. Kennedy was killed on November 22, 1963, in Dallas, Texas.
469c386c: Which liner sank on its maiden voyage in April 1912?
The Titanic hit an iceberg on the night of April 14-15, 1912. More than 1,500 people died.
1d721c99: Who led the Salt March in India in 1930?
To protest the British salt monopoly, Gandhi walked nearly 400 km to the sea.
e72e2344: In what year did India gain independence?
India became independent on August 15, 1947. Partition also created Pakistan.
ad69bda6: Which dynasty ruled Russia from 1613 to 1917?
The Romanovs ruled for more than 300 years, until Nicholas II's abdication in 1917.
52542785: Which treaty signed in 1957 created the European Economic Community?
The Treaty of Rome, signed by six countries including France and West Germany, created the EEC, forerunner of the European Union.
c26cc0b8: In what year were euro coins and banknotes put into circulation?
The euro has existed for banks since 1999, but coins and notes arrived in people's wallets on January 1, 2002.
c72c831e: In which country is the Chernobyl power plant, site of the 1986 accident?
On April 26, 1986, a reactor at the Chernobyl plant in Soviet Ukraine exploded, the worst civilian nuclear disaster.
5a6daece: Which people built the citadel of Machu Picchu, in the Andes?
Machu Picchu, in Peru, was built by the Incas in the 15th century. It was brought to the world's attention in 1911.
e337eb32: Which 1962 crisis nearly triggered a nuclear war between the United States and the USSR?
In October 1962, Soviet missiles were discovered in Cuba. After thirteen days of tension, the USSR agreed to withdraw them.
12f3ff34: Which military alliance was created in 1949 around the United States and European countries?
The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was founded in 1949 to protect Western Europe against the USSR.
09d3eefa: Which military alliance brought together the USSR and its allies from 1955?
The Warsaw Pact, signed in 1955, was a response to West Germany joining NATO. It was dissolved in 1991.
f536f1dc: Which Soviet leader launched perestroika and glasnost?
Coming to power in 1985, Mikhail Gorbachev launched economic reforms (perestroika) and political openness (glasnost).
413eb5f5: Along which parallel is Korea divided in two?
Since 1945, Korea has been split in two around the 38th parallel. The Korean War (1950-1953) did not change this division.
d8c0aa6a: How was West Berlin supplied during the Soviet blockade of 1948-1949?
For almost a year, American and British planes flew food and coal to the people of West Berlin.
81afa72b: Which American president declared “Ich bin ein Berliner” in 1963?
On June 26, 1963, before the people of West Berlin, Kennedy declared his solidarity with the city divided by the Wall.
65e21b18: Which war ended with the fall of Saigon in 1975?
On April 30, 1975, North Vietnamese troops entered Saigon. Vietnam was reunified the following year.
015b072d: For which event was the Eiffel Tower built?
Gustave Eiffel's tower was inaugurated for the 1889 World's Fair, the centenary of the Revolution.
fa23cded: Which queen reigned over the United Kingdom for more than 70 years?
Elizabeth II reigned from 1952 until her death in 2022, more than 70 years, a record for a British monarch.
